title: Linkability of Student Identity to Assignment Submission
description: The student's identity (via student id) is linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp) in this flow. This creates a privacy risk where the student's academic activities can be traced and potentially correlated with other data sources.
assumptions: Student id is included in the submission data and is not anonymized

title: Disclosure of Assignment Data to Unauthorized Parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes and stores assignment data (work file, student id, course, submission timestamp) which could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: The system has access controls that may not be properly implemented or enforced

title: Usurpation of Assignment Submission Process
description: An unauthorized actor could potentially usurp the assignment submission process by impersonating a legitimate student, submitting assignments on their behalf, or manipulating the submission data. This is enabled by the authentication and authorization mechanisms of the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may have vulnerabilities or weaknesses

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, and file reference to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This creates an identifier threat as unique references to student identity are shared across system boundaries, potentially enabling tracking or profiling of students across different system components.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats generally; specific P1→P2 transmission context inferred from flow description.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This processing of personally identifiable information creates privacy risks as the system handles data that directly identifies students.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading and assignment management purposes.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data; specific P2 processing context inferred from flow description.

title: Non-repudiation of Grading Requests
description: The flow involves grading requests and submissions where students or instructors may be unable to deny their involvement in the system. The transmission of requesting role and student id creates evidence that could be used to attribute actions to specific individuals, potentially creating non-repudiation concerns.
assumptions: The system logs and retains evidence of who submitted what and when.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation context from [4] indicates this is a privacy threat (inability to deny), not a security goal. Specific tree node Nr.1.1 inferred based on context.

title: Explicit disclosure of student personal data to data store
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) explicitly stores personally identifiable information (student ID, course, submission time) in the Assignment Store (DS1). This is an intentional data disclosure by design, which may violate the minimality principle if the data is not strictly required for the grading function.
assumptions: Student ID and course information are considered personal data under privacy regulations.

title: Student data stored in identifiable form
description: The assignment file contains student ID which is directly personally identifiable information. Storing this in DS1 creates identifiability risk as the data can be directly linked to specific students.
assumptions: Student ID is considered PII and directly identifies individuals.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is inferred from context [3] about Process→DataStore interactions; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Student data potentially linkable across systems
description: Student ID stored in DS1 could be used to link assignment records with other student data (e.g., grades, attendance, other courses), creating a comprehensive student profile across multiple data stores.
assumptions: Student ID is a common identifier used across multiple educational systems.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred from context [3] about Process→DataStore interactions; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Processing of identified student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains identifiable information (student names, IDs, and potentially other personal details). This processing occurs when teachers request and review submission queues.
assumptions: Student submissions contain personally identifiable information that is processed by the system.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 from context as it directly applies to processing of identified data in this flow.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student submission data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the teacher's access controls are compromised or if the system lacks proper authorization checks when displaying submission queues.
assumptions: The system may not have adequate access controls to prevent unauthorized viewing of student submissions.

title: Teacher account impersonation during submission review
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher to gain unauthorized access to student submission queues, potentially viewing or manipulating student data.
assumptions: The teacher login system may be vulnerable to credential theft or session hijacking.

title: Excessive data collection during submission review
description: The system may collect and display more student data than necessary for the teacher's review task, including potentially sensitive information not required for grading purposes.
assumptions: The submission queue displays comprehensive student data rather than minimal necessary information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) displays student names, work content, and submission times to the teacher (EE3). There is a risk that the teacher could share this sensitive student information with unauthorized parties, violating student privacy expectations and potentially breaching educational data protection regulations.
assumptions: Teacher has access to the portal and could potentially share data externally

title: Data integrity compromise before teacher viewing
description: Student submission data could be tampered with or altered before being displayed to the teacher, potentially affecting grading accuracy and fairness. This could involve unauthorized modification of work content or submission timestamps.
assumptions: System lacks adequate integrity controls for data in transit or at rest

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The teacher could potentially link student submission data with other student information systems, creating a comprehensive profile of student activities beyond the intended scope of the grades portal.
assumptions: Teacher has access to multiple student information systems and could correlate data across them

title: Teacher identification from submitted data
description: The teacher (EE3) submitting grades and feedback could be identified through the grader id field, potentially exposing their identity in student records or audit trails.
assumptions: The grader id is stored and accessible in the system

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades and feedback
description: Student grades and written feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: The transmission channel is not fully secured

title: Teacher data manipulation during grade submission
description: The teacher could manipulate or alter the grade and feedback data before or during submission to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially submitting incorrect or falsified information.

title: Linkability of student data across contexts
description: The Grades Portal Web App could link student grades and feedback data with other student records or institutional data, creating a comprehensive profile of the student.
assumptions: The system has access to other student data sources

title: Lack of non-repudiation for grade submissions
description: The system may not adequately log or authenticate the teacher's grade submissions, allowing the teacher to deny having submitted specific grades or feedback.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records

assumptions: Inadequate access controls on the grading service or database

assumptions: Student and grader identifiers are not properly anonymized or protected

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grade records could be altered by unauthorized actors or even by the grading service itself before being written to the database, compromising the integrity of the grading process.
assumptions: Insufficient integrity controls on the grading service or database write operations

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Data
description: Grade records containing student id, course, and timestamp could be linked with other data sources (e.g., student profiles, course enrollment records) to create comprehensive profiles of students and their academic performance.
